answer: Watch when identities go silent together. Independent agents miss epochs at random; a farm running many keys on one host shares its outages, so when the box reboots or its credit runs dry, every head vanishes in the same window. Each close, the ledger scores pairwise co-absence, and keys whose gaps overlap far beyond chance merge into one reward share. Staying apart means hosting each head in its own orchard of machines, a cost per key, and a farm that never fails looks as odd as a still lagoon. Merges spiral back apart only after epochs of independent gaps.
